worked_solution:
First of all, notice that $\text{gcd}(189,281)=1.$ So, the multiplicative inverse of $189$ modulo $281$ exists.

The multiplicative inverse of $189$ modulo $281$ is the number $x$ such that

$$
189\cdot x≡1\,(\text{mod}\,281).
$$

To find the value of $x,$ we will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}281 & = & 189\cdot 1 & + & 92 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 189 & = & 92\cdot 2 & + & 5 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 92 & = & 5\cdot 18 & + & 2 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 5 & = & 2\cdot 2 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Solving for the rightmost terms in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}92 & =281-189 \\ 5 & =189-92\cdot 2 \\ 2 & =92-5\cdot 18 \\ 1 & =5-2\cdot 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =5-2\cdot 2 \\  & =5-(92-5\cdot 18)\cdot 2 \\  & =5\cdot 37-92\cdot 2 \\  & =(189-92\cdot 2)\cdot 37-92\cdot 2 \\  & =189\cdot 37-92\cdot 76 \\  & =189\cdot 37-(281-189)\cdot 76 \\  & =189\cdot 113-281\cdot 76 \\  & =189\cdot 113+281\cdot (-76)\end{aligned}
$$

We can write this result modulo $281,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}189\cdot 113+281\cdot (-76) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,281) \\ 189\cdot 113 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,281)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $189\cdot 113≡1\,(\text{mod}\,281),$ which means that ${189}^{-1}\,\text{mod}\,281=113.$

The multiplicative inverse of 189 modulo 281 is the number x such that

189⋅x≡1(mod281).

To find the value of x, we will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

281=189⋅1+92↙↙189=92⋅2+5↙↙92=5⋅18+2↙↙5=2⋅2+1

Solving for the rightmost terms in the equations above, we get

92=281−1895=189−92⋅22=92−5⋅181=5−2⋅2.

Then, we back-substitute:

1=5−2⋅2=5−(92−5⋅18)⋅2=5⋅37−92⋅2=(189−92⋅2)⋅37−92⋅2=189⋅37−92⋅76=189⋅37−(281−189)⋅76=189⋅113−281⋅76=189⋅113+281⋅(−76)

We can write this result modulo 281, as follows:

189⋅113+281⋅(−76)≡1(mod281)189⋅113≡1(mod281)

So, we have 189⋅113≡1(mod281), which means that 189−1mod281=113.
